background.speaker: SPEAKER_00
background.text: We reported on that committee hearing yesterday, and one thing that you said, you warned against imposing new regulations, government regulations on the airlines. Why was that important? And do you think that that message was received? Do Democrats feel the same way, who control the Senate?

ground_truth: So not all of them. Listen, what happened with Southwest, there were millions of passengers who were delayed or stranded over Christmas because Southwest. And I've spoken with the senior leadership of Southwest. They've admitted they screwed up. They screwed up, it was unacceptable, and a lot of people were severely inconvenienced as a result of it. That's frustrating. At the same time, I recognize Southwest is a great Texas company. I fly Southwest probably every single week. I joke, I call Southwest the company plane because I'm on their plane so often. And I think most days Southwest Airlines does a phenomenal job of getting you where you need to go, doing so in an inexpensive manner so that air travel is affordable, and doing so with a smile. I like that the Southwest flight attendants are as likely to pick up the microphone and start singing a jingle into the microphone. So they do it. A lot of things well. And so I approached the hearing this week. I wanted to make sure it wasn't just an excuse for Democrats to beat up on Southwest. Yes, they screwed up. Yes, they need to make customers whole. And I was very glad to see that Southwest has been proactive, leaning forward to refunding people flights, to giving them 25,000 frequent flyer miles, to leaning in and covering costs that people incurred. All of those were the right things to do. But I didn't want it to become, just Democrats treating Southwest like a pinata and taking shots at them, and I also don't want what happened there to become an excuse for the Biden administration re-regulating aviation. Used to be that the commercial airlines were very heavily regulated. Prices were very heavily regulated. And when that happened, they were really expensive. Many people couldn't afford to buy a plane ticket because it was very expensive. We had tremendous success in this country when we deregulated the airlines and allowed price competition. And it's actually what led to the rise of low cost carriers like Southwest that drive down costs for everyone else. And so my view of the regulatory mission when it comes to aviation is on safety, we shouldn't compromise. And on the FAA, we need to ensure the FAA is imposing serious standards to keep the flying public safe. That's the number one obligation of the regulators. But what we shouldn't be doing is letting Democrats set prices and micromanage and determine how many drink tickets is Jack Fink gonna get when he gets on the next plane? You know what, that's not a question for the government to answer. I think the free market works pretty well on that.
